column3: The Greek says “His paths,” rendered as “paths for Him.”
“All humanity” renders the Greek image “all flesh.”
The Greek has plural “fruits,” rather than collective singular “fruit.”
The Greek uses present passive verbs for cutting and throwing; BSB uses future forms.
“Money” makes the object of extortion explicit; the Greek separately prohibits extortion and false accusation.
The Greek says “comes” in the present, rather than “will come.”
The Greek makes Herod the subject being rebuked, while BSB makes the rebuker the active subject; the name Herod is repeated in the Greek last clause.
“His ministry” supplies the unspecified object of “began.”
